_comment: Achievable-peak calibration for Ascend910B3 (20 AIC / 40 AIV, 1800 MHz, L2 192 MB, HBM 64 GB),
Why this file exists: the framework's Ratio divides by a THEORETICAL peak
(bw = 1.75 TB/s, Computility ~ 4.6 TOp/s), which is physically unreachable, so Ratio
cannot answer 'how much head-room is left'. Head-room must be measured against the
达成率 is therefore computed from absolute quantities, never from a nominal percentage:
Re-calibrate after a toolchain upgrade or on a different device.
Probe: 3 reads + 1 write vadd over GM (bandwidth) / UB-resident 4-way vadd (compute),

nominal._comment: values msprof uses as the Ratio denominator (SoC lookup + ppc arithmetic). Reference only - do NOT use as a head-room denominator.

caliber_notes._comment: DECIDED 2026-11-09: report Ratio with the 1.75 denominator. Do not switch without the three prerequisites below.
adopted_because: it is the value msprof actually reports on Ascend910B3 (read back from visualize_data.bin bw field), so anyone can reproduce it
all 82 existing benchmark.md reports were produced with it, so historical comparisons stay valid

rejected_alternatives.1.64: claimed by an uncommitted orphan doc (docs/optimize_results_20261030.md) as DEVICE_GM_BW_TBPS / SOC_CONFIG['Ascend910B3']. Verified absent from both HEAD and the working tree - no code implements it, and CONST-ascend910-9362-profile is not registered in pattern-library. Do not adopt until: (1) the constant is actually committed to benchmark_base.py + msprof_roofline.py, (2) the historical reports are re-run under the new caliber, (3) the device constant is registered in pattern-library.
rejected_alternatives.1.8: the Ascend910B2C value recorded in docs/roofline_metrics_analysis.md; wrong device for this machine

caliber_notes.impact_if_switched_to_1_64: Ratio scales by 1.75/1.64 = 1.067 (+6.7%). This flips borderline verdicts: ErfFwdOp 59.02% -> 63.0% (would pass the 60% line). Never mix calibers inside one report.
caliber_notes.head_room_denominator: neither 1.75 nor 1.64 - always use the measured achievable peaks in this file (1.062~1.490 TB/s bandwidth, 2.97/3.494 TOp/s compute)

averaging_rule._comment: CONFIRMED by the team 2026-11-09. Use this when reporting a single pass/fail number per operator.
averaging_rule.exclude_smoke_reason: the 1M smoke workloads carry ~3.75 us of fixed launch overhead (36% of their latency), which depresses every operator's mean by 8~12pt. The repository's own tuning flow already excludes them - see perf_opt/opt_log.md: 'smoke 排除出性能调优, 仅作精度回归'. Excluding them moved 5/20 to 8/20 pass.
averaging_rule.pick_rule: when both the team report and a local measurement exist, take the HIGHER mean per operator
averaging_rule.still_report_separately: smoke-1m values must remain visible in the report as an observation column; they represent a real small-shape scenario, they are simply not scored

achievable_bandwidth_TBs._comment: DRAM-side (framework Perf/AI) achievable bandwidth, with the implied Ratio ceiling vs the 1.75 nominal.

measured.note: bin L2 counter invalid at this size; derived from declared_bytes / duration

achievable_bandwidth_TBs.traffic_mix_caveat: probe is 3-read-1-write. A 1-read-1-write op sees a slightly lower ceiling (BitwiseNotFwdOp 1R1W reached 1.395 TB/s at 16M vs 1.490 for the 3R1W probe), so the tier value is an upper bound and 达成率 can slightly exceed 100% for a different traffic mix.

achievable_compute_TOpss._comment: achievable vector compute throughput in absolute TOp/s. Use Perf (TOp/s) directly against this.

cross_check.note: a real saturated kernel beats the UB-bound probe at fp32 by 54%; 2.97 is the better fp32 bound. float16 has no saturated kernel cross-check yet, so 3.494 is probe-only (low confidence).

startup_overhead.basis: Erf 1M latency minus 16M/16; consistent across fp32/fp16/bf16 (36% of the 1M latency)
startup_overhead.exclusion_rule: exclude a workload from the pass/fail average when (t_small - t_large*N_small/N_large)/t_small > 0.30, but still report it separately

measurement_noise.comment: two probes, 6 and 8 launches; the 3% noise threshold in the skill is conservative
